title: Equal opportunity and respectful work
moduleTitle: Shared: Job management and service delivery
audience: Any owner, supervisor or worker in a service business who recruits, supervises or works alongside other people.
learningOutcomes: Describe respectful behaviour and the forms of discrimination and harassment that the business must prevent.
Identify what to do when a worker or customer experiences discrimination or harassment.
Explain why the business's equal opportunity obligations must be checked for each state and territory.

instruction.heading: Respectful work
instruction.body: Respectful work means that each person is treated fairly, without being excluded, mocked or disadvantaged because of who they are or what they believe. In a service business the team works in other people's homes and sites, so the way the team treats each other is seen by customers. Respect covers how a worker talks to a colleague, how a supervisor gives feedback, and how a worker responds to a customer's request. It also covers the sharing of tasks, shifts and access to training.

instruction.heading: Discrimination and harassment
instruction.body: Discrimination is treating a person less favourably because of an attribute the law protects, such as sex, race, disability, age, religion or family status, depending on the law that applies. Harassment is unwelcome conduct that a reasonable person would expect to offend, humiliate or intimidate. Both can occur between workers, between a worker and a customer, or between a worker and a third party. The protected attributes and the rules differ between Commonwealth and state and territory laws, and must be confirmed for the location and the business.

instruction.heading: What to do when it happens
instruction.body: A worker who experiences or sees discrimination or harassment should be able to raise it through a clear route. The business should take the concern seriously, record the facts, protect the person from further harm and deal with the matter through its procedure. Do not retaliate against a person who raises a concern in good faith. Where the conduct is serious or may be unlawful, the person may also contact the relevant state or territory or Commonwealth body; the bodies and their processes must be confirmed for the location and have not yet been confirmed in this lesson.

procedure: Treat each colleague and customer with fairness and respect in all communication and tasks.
Share tasks, shifts and training fairly, and base decisions on the work and the rules.
If discrimination or harassment is seen or reported, record the facts and tell the designated contact.
Protect the person from further harm and do not retaliate against a good-faith complaint.
Deal with the matter through the business's procedure and record the outcome.
Check the protected attributes and the reporting bodies for the state or territory before relying on them.

workedExamples.situation: A supervisor repeatedly gives the most physically demanding jobs to one worker because of their age, and makes comments about it in front of the team.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What should a team member do?
workedExamples.reasoning: Record the facts, including the dates, the jobs allocated and the comments. Raise the concern through the designated contact or the business's complaint route. The business should review the allocation on the basis of the work and the rules, and check the legal position for the state or territory.

commonErrors.error: Dismissing a concern as a joke or as a personal matter.
commonErrors.prevention: Record the facts and raise the concern through the approved route.

commonErrors.error: Retaliating against a worker who raised a concern.
commonErrors.prevention: Protect the worker and deal with the concern through the procedure.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Anti-discrimination and harassment laws apply at the Commonwealth, state and territory levels, with different protected attributes and reporting bodies.
Psychological and physical safety at work is part of the work health and safety duty. Harassment that creates a risk to a worker's health or safety must be managed under the WHS framework as well.

qualityStandard: Work is allocated on the basis of the work and the rules, and recorded.
Every concern raised is recorded and dealt with through the procedure.
No worker is disadvantaged for raising a concern in good faith.
documentationEvidence: Complaint record with the facts, the action taken and the outcome.
Record of work allocation decisions where the business keeps one.
summary: Treat everyone with fairness and respect in work and in customer contact.
Record and raise concerns of discrimination or harassment through the approved route.
Protect the person from retaliation; confirm the legal obligations for the location.

knowledgeChecks.question: A worker raises a concern about being treated unfairly. What should the business do?
options: Dismiss it as a personal matter and remove the worker from the next job and the roster
Tell the worker to stop complaining and that they will be moved to a different site
Record the facts, deal with it through the procedure and protect the worker from retaliation.

knowledgeChecks.question: What decides which attributes are protected from discrimination?
options: The applicable Commonwealth, state or territory law, which must be checked.
The business's preference, recorded in its own staff handbook
What customers think about the service, and the price they pay

knowledgeChecks.question: What is discrimination, according to the lesson?
options: Asking a person about their weekend
Treating a person less favourably because of an attribute the law protects
